answer: SybilRank bounds fake-identity influence by launching short random walks of length O(log V) from an audited beacon seed set across the bilateral attestation graph and ranking nodes by degree-normalized landing probability. In rapid-mixing honest regions, a legitimate walk disperses like a zephyr across well-connected peers, whereas any walk crossing the sparse attack edge into a Sybil cluster stays trapped as an internal echo and divides that fixed escaped probability mass across all k clones, capping per-fake trust at O(g/k) unless the operator wins k real attack edges.
